concerns.text: T013 implements filtering via 'BFS/DFS traversal from the issue target files' but fails to implement the spec's FR-001 requirement to determine 'relevant file history' via 'static analysis of the issue description'. The task assumes target files are known inputs, whereas the spec requires the system to *derive* the starting nodes of the graph from the issue text itself. This is a semantic weakening of the filtering logic.

T026 mentions 'handling memory pressure via aggressive quantization' for the 7B model. The plan's 'Complexity Tracking' explicitly rejects using different quantization levels to avoid confounding 'Model Size' with 'Quantization Noise', mandating Q4_K_M for *all* models. Allowing 'aggressive' (implied lower than Q4) quantization violates the experimental control defined in the plan.

T030 implements post-hoc comparisons to identify if '1B-model (high-fidelity) outperforms 7B-model (baseline)'. However, the task description does not explicitly restrict the comparison to *only* the high-fidelity 1B vs. baseline 7B configuration. It risks allowing invalid cross-strategy comparisons (e.g., 1B-Baseline vs 7B-High-Fidelity) which do not test the specific hypothesis in SC-004, weakening the acceptance criterion.

T029 implements a 'GLM' but omits the 'GLMM or Firth's GLM' logic justified in the plan's 'Complexity Tracking' section for handling sparse binary data (low Pass@1 rates). The plan explicitly states standard GLM 'fails to converge' in this regime. Implementing a standard GLM without the Firth correction or Mixed Model logic violates the methodological constraint required to answer the research question.

T022 implements 'rule-based semantic summarization' by extracting 'first sentence of each paragraph AND last sentence of each function block'. The plan's 'Complexity Tracking' section explicitly REJECTS this 'first/last sentence' heuristic, stating it 'discards critical logic, invalidating the high-fidelity construct'. Implementing the rejected heuristic violates the plan's design decision.
